questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Unit Tangent Vector at an Arbitrary Point
questions.problem:
Which of the following gives the unit tangent vector to the curve
 $r(t)=⟨2t,\,4\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )?$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),\,y(t),\,z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{sin}⁡2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,8\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,-8\operatorname{sin}⁡2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(2)}^{2}+(8\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)^{2}+{(-8\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+64{cos}^{2}⁡2t+64{sin}^{2}⁡2t} \\  & =2\sqrt{1+16({cos}^{2}⁡2t+{sin}^{2}⁡2t)} \\  & =2\sqrt{1+16} \\  & =2\sqrt{17}\end{aligned}
$$

 Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{17}}⟨2,\,8\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,-8\operatorname{sin}⁡2t⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}⟨1,\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,-4\operatorname{sin}⁡2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,j \\  & =i+2t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+4{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4{t}^{2}}}(\,i+2t\,j)\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨t\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),\,y(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{sin}^{2}⁡t+2t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{t}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡t+4{cos}^{2}⁡t-2t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{t}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{4({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)+{t}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\sqrt{4+{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{4+{t}^{2}}}⟨2\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=\sqrt{t}\,i+(2-t)\,j$ at an arbitrary point where $t\in (0,\infty ).$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2-t)\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,i-\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}})}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{4t}+1} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1+4t}{4t}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{1+4t}}{2\sqrt{t}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{t}}{\sqrt{1+4t}}(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}i-\,j) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4t}}(i-2\sqrt{t}\,j)\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}{t}^{2}⟩$ at the point where $t=\pi .$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\pi :$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot 2t⟩ \\  & =⟨t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\sqrt{3}t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\pi ) & =⟨\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,\sqrt{3}\pi ⟩ \\  & =⟨-\pi ,\,0,\,\sqrt{3}\pi ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(\pi ):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖ & =\sqrt{(-\pi )^{2}+(0)^{2}+(\sqrt{3}\pi )^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{\pi }^{2}} \\  & =2\pi \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(\pi )$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at the point where $t=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\pi ) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(\pi )}{‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }⟨-\pi ,\,0,\,\sqrt{3}\pi ⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{2},\,0,\,\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: What is the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨{t}^{4},\,{t}^{2},\,4t⟩$ at the point $P(1,1,4)?$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(1,1,4)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨1,\,1,\,4⟩ \\ ⟨{t}^{4},\,{t}^{2},\,4t⟩ & =⟨1,\,1,\,4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}{t}^{4}=1 \\ {t}^{2}=1 \\ 4t=4.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equality, we get $t=1.$ This value satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, the point $P(1,1,4)$ is at the tip of $r(1).$  

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t)⟩ \\  & =⟨4{t}^{3},\,2t,\,4⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =⟨4(1)^{3},\,2(1),\,4⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,2,\,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36} \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(1,1,4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(1)}{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}⟨4,\,2,\,4⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{3},\,\frac{1}{3},\,\frac{2}{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: What is the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k$ at the point $P(2\pi ,1,0)?$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)\,j+y(t)\,j+z(t)\,k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by 

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(2\pi ,1,0)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =2\pi \,i+\,j+0\,k \\ t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k & =2\pi \,i+\,j+0\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}t=2\pi  \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t=1 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t=0.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=2\pi .$ This value also satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, the point $P(2\pi ,1,0)$ is at the tip of $r(2\pi ).$  

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=2\pi :$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,k \\  & =i-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,k \\ {r}^{′}(2\pi ) & =\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )\,k \\  & =i+0\,j+\,k \\  & =i+k\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(2\pi ):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(2\pi )‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+0+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(2\pi )$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(2\pi ,1,0):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(2\pi ) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(2\pi )}{‖{r}^{′}(2\pi )‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot (i+k) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,i+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: What is the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=2t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+t\,k$ at the point $P(2,1,1)?$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)\,j+y(t)\,j+z(t)\,k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by 

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(2,1,1)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =2\,i+\,j+\,k \\ 2t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+t\,k & =2\,i+\,j+\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2t=2 \\ {t}^{2}=1 \\ t=1.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=1.$ This value satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, the point $P(2,1,1)$ is at the tip of $r(1).$ 

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,k \\  & =2\,i+2t\,j+\,k \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =2\,i+2(1)\,j+\,k \\  & =2\,i+2\,j+\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}+1} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(2,1,1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(1)}{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(2\,i+2\,j+\,k) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\,i+\frac{2}{3}\,j+\frac{1}{3}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: What is the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+2{t}^{2}\,k$ at the point $P(2,4,8)?$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)\,j+y(t)\,j+z(t)\,k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(2,4,8)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =2\,i+4\,j+8\,k \\ t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+2{t}^{2}\,k & =2\,i+4\,j+8\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}t=2 \\ {t}^{2}=4 \\ 2{t}^{2}=8.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=2.$ This value also satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, the point $P(2,4,8)$ is at the tip of $r(2).$ 

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2})\,k \\  & =i+2t\,j+4t\,k \\ {r}^{′}(2) & =\,i+2\cdot 2\,j+4\cdot 2\,k \\  & =i+4\,j+8\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(2)‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{8}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{81} \\  & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(2)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(2,4,8):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(2) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(2)}{‖{r}^{′}(2)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\cdot (i+4\,j+8\,k) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\,i+\frac{4}{9}\,j+\frac{8}{9}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=({t}^{2}-2t)p(t)$ at the point corresponding to $t=1$, given that  $p(1)=i+2\,j-k\,$ and $\,{p}^{′}(1)=2\,i-\,j-2\,k.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(({t}^{2}-2t)p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-2t)\cdot p(t)+({t}^{2}-2t)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =(2t-2)\,p(t)+({t}^{2}-2t)\,{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =(2(1)-2)\,p(1)+((1)^{2}-2(1))\,{p}^{′}(1) \\  & =0-{p}^{′}(1) \\  & =-(2\,i-\,j-2\,k) \\  & =-2i+\,j+2k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}‖r(1)‖ & =\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+(1)^{2}+(2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(1)}{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot (-2\,i+j+2k) \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}\,i+\frac{1}{3}\,j+\frac{2}{3}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=1$ is  $T(1)=-\frac{2}{3}\,i+\frac{1}{3}\,j+\frac{2}{3}\,k.$

questions.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=({t}^{2}+2)p(t)$ at the point corresponding to $t=-1$, given that  $p(-1)=i+2\,j-k\,$ and $\,{p}^{′}(-1)=i+\,j-\,k.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=-1:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(({t}^{2}+2)p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+2)\cdot p(t)+({t}^{2}+2)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =2t\,p(t)+({t}^{2}+2)\,{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(-1) & =2(-1)\,p(-1)+((-1)^{2}+2)\,{p}^{′}(-1) \\  & =-2\,p(-1)+3\,{p}^{′}(-1) \\  & =-2(i+2\,j-k)+3(i+\,j-\,k) \\  & =-2i-4\,j+2k+3i+3j-3\,k \\  & =i-j-k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}‖r(1)‖ & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(-1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(-1)}{‖{r}^{′}(-1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot (i-j-k) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}(i-j-k)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=-1$ is  $T(-1)=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}(i-j-k).$

questions.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,p(t)$ at the point corresponding to $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$, given that  $p(\frac{\pi }{4})=\,i-\,j+2k\,$ and $\,{p}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})=\,i+\,j.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{4}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\cdot p(t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,p(t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})p(\frac{\pi }{4})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}){p}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(i-\,j+2k)+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(i+\,j) \\  & =\sqrt{2}(i+k)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖ & =\sqrt{(\sqrt{2})^{2}+(0)^{2}+(\sqrt{2})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})}{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \sqrt{2}(i+k) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(i+k)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$ is
 $T(\frac{\pi }{4})=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(i+k).$

questions.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=\operatorname{tan}⁡t\,p(t)$ at the point corresponding to $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$, given that  $p(\frac{\pi }{4})=i-\frac{3}{2}\,j+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,k\,$ and $\,{p}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})=\sqrt{3}\,k.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{4}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{tan}⁡t\,p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{tan}⁡t)\cdot p(t)+\operatorname{tan}⁡t\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡t\,p(t)+\operatorname{tan}⁡t\,{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & ={sec}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})p(\frac{\pi }{4})+\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}){p}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =2(i-\frac{3}{2}\,j+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,k)+(1)(\sqrt{3}\,k) \\  & =(2\,i-3\,j+\sqrt{3}\,k)+\sqrt{3}\,k \\  & =2\,i-3\,j+2\sqrt{3}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖r(\frac{\pi }{4})‖ & =\sqrt{(2)^{2}+(-3)^{2}+(2\sqrt{3})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+9+12} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})}{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot (2\,i-3\,j+2\sqrt{3}\,k) \\  & =\frac{2}{5}\,i-\frac{3}{5}\,j+\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{5}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$ is
 $T(\frac{\pi }{4})=\frac{2}{5}\,i-\frac{3}{5}\,j+\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{5}\,k.$

questions.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)={e}^{-t}p(t)$ at the point where $t=0$, if $p(0)=\,i+\,j+k$ and ${p}^{′}(0)=\,i-\,j.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t}p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t})p(t)+{e}^{-t}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =-{e}^{-t}p(t)+{e}^{-t}{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(0) & =-{e}^{0}p(0)+{e}^{0}{p}^{′}(0) \\  & =-(\,i+\,j+k)+(\,i-\,j) \\  & =-2j-k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(0)‖ & =\sqrt{(0)^{2}+(-2)^{2}+(1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{0+4+1} \\  & =\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(0)}{‖{r}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}(-2j-k) \\  & =-\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}j-\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=0$ is $T(0)=-\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}j-\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}k.$

canonical_examples.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $\mathbf r(t)=\left\langle \sin^3{t}, \:\cos^3{t} \right\rangle$ at an arbitrary point where $0 < t < \dfrac{\pi}{2}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
For a curve $\mathbf r(t)= x(t) \,\mathbf i + y(t) \,\mathbf j,$ the unit tangent vector $\mathbf T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t))$ is given by 

$$
\mathbf T(t)=\dfrac{\mathbf r'(t)}{\left\| \mathbf r'(t) \right\|}.
$$

First, we find the derivative of $\mathbf r(t)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({sin}^{3}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({cos}^{3}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨3{sin}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,3{cos}^{2}⁡t(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of $\mathbf r'(t)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =|3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t|\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡t+(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\ \text{ } & =|3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t|\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =|3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t|\sqrt{1} \\  & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

 

In the last step, we were able to remove the absolute value bars because $\sin{t}>0$ and $\cos{t}>0$ for $0 < t < \dfrac{\pi}{2}.$

Finally, we normalize $\mathbf r'(t)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩}{3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t} \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $\mathbf r(t)=e^{2t}\mathbf p(t)$ at the point where $t=0,$ if $\mathbf p(0)=\mathbf i-\,\mathbf j-\mathbf k$ and $\mathbf p'(0)=\mathbf i - \mathbf j+ 2\mathbf k.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
For a curve $\mathbf r(t)=x(t)\mathbf i+y(t)\mathbf j+z(t)\mathbf k,$ the unit tangent vector $\mathbf T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
\mathbf T(t)=\dfrac{\mathbf r'(t)}{\left\| \mathbf r'(t) \right\|}.
$$

First, we find $\mathbf r'(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t}p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t})p(t)+{e}^{2t}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =2{e}^{2t}p(t)+{e}^{2t}{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(0) & =2{e}^{2(0)}p(0)+{e}^{2(0)}{p}^{′}(0) \\  & =2(i-\,j-k)+1(i-j+2k) \\  & =3\,i-3\,j\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we calculate the magnitude of $\mathbf r'(0)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(0)‖ & =\sqrt{(3)^{2}+(-3)^{2}+(0)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2\cdot {3}^{2}} \\  & =3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize $\mathbf r'(0)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(0)}{‖{r}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}(3\,i-3\,j) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(i-j) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(i-j)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=0$ is $\mathbf T(0) = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(\mathbf i -  \mathbf j).$
